summary: Steel fire tower in Lee County, listed among seven new steel towers erected in the state's 1937-38 report and marked removed on Eastern US Lookouts; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Eastern US Lookouts marks the tower Removed, with no date or method given.

events.note: The state report for July 1937 to June 1938 lists Bishopville among seven new steel fire towers erected that year. Year given is the one the report period ends in.

evidence.supports: Bishopville was one of seven new steel fire towers erected in the 1937-38 report year
evidence.quote: Seven new steel fire towers were erected, including Bishopville in Lee County.

evidence.supports: The Civilian Conservation Corps built towers and telephone lines that year at no cost to the state or protective associations
evidence.quote: Additional towers and telephone lines were constructed during the year by the Civilian Conservation Corps at no cost to the State or protective associations.

evidence.supports: Support buildings at five tower sites, Bishopville one of them: dwelling, barn, smoke house, chicken house, latrine
evidence.quote: Tower unit buildings consisting of a four room dwelling, barn, smoke house, chicken house and latrine were constructed at five tower sites. Bishopville being one of these sites.

evidence.supports: Eastern US Lookouts marks the Bishopville tower as removed
South Carolina phased out its towers in the early 1990s
evidence.quote: South Carolina phased out its towers in the early 1990s. Today, only 30 of them remain standing.

evidence.supports: The article ties more than 100 towers around the state closing to a 1993 change at the Forestry Commission
evidence.quote: Martin, 52, of Eutaw Springs, lost the lookout job in 1993 as the Forestry Commission moved into a new era and more than 100 towers around the state closed.

sources.title: Looking out for last fire towers

notes_for_editor: Built and removal facts come only from the Eastern US Lookouts page, which quotes the state forestry report; the original report was not read directly. No staffing, access, fire or visit data found. Search hits for a Bishopville tower mostly pointed to WAGS-AM (TopoQuest place 1252314, N34.210155 W80.230350, about 8 km from the brief coordinates), a broadcast tower, so it was not used. The brief coordinates 34.2279, -80.3065 are not verified by any source here. The state report's Bishopville entry is the only source on the 1937-38 build. The statewide Post and Courier figures are context, not Bishopville-specific. The Forestry Commission's 'Pictures From Our Past' page was not checked (not reached within budget).
